full_judgment:
6. Mr. Khandakar Saiful Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellant submitted that in fact there was no legal evidence to prove that deceased Shahida Khatun was the wife of sole appellant Labai, therefore, the impugned judgment and order of conviction passed by the court below on the wrong premise that the appellant being the husband absconded himself and thus failed to explain as to how his wife, the deceased had met with the death. He further submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge was totally wrong in relying upon the statements of the two witnesses, namely, p.w.s. 10 and 17 allegedly made before the Magistrate 1st class under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the same were not recorded in accordance with law and further the said witnesses while deposed in court being recalled by the court did not own their said statements and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable in law and the appellant is entitled to be acquitted and the appeal be allowed. 

 7. Mr. Golam Kibria, the learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the State on the other hand, submitted that although the First Information Report is not the substantive evidence, yet p.w.1, the informant having clearly stated in the First Information Report that 17/18 days before of the alleged occurrence Shaheda was married to accused Labai and if the same is read with the statements of p.w.17 made before the Upazilla Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure visavis the suggestion given to him by the prosecution in cross examination after he was declared hostile it was proved beyond all reasonable doubt that deceased Shaheda was the wife of accused-appellant Labai, therefore, he was obliged to explain as to how his wife had met with the death, which he failed, the court below rightly found him guilty of the charge under section 302 of the Penal Code and no interference is called for by this court with the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 20. These are all the evidence on record adduced by the prosecution. 

 21. From the impugned judgment it appears that in fact the learned Additional Sessions Judge found the sole appellant guilty under section 302 of the Penal Code relying on the suggestion given by the prosecution in cross examination to p.ws. 17 and 10 respectively with reference to their statements allegedly made by them before the Upazilla Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure after they were declared hostile on being recalled suo-moto by him. It is to be noted, that these two p.ws. were tendered by the prosecution and the defence declined to cross-examine them. From the evidence of the other p.ws.as reproduced hereinbefore it is clear that none of the p.ws. deposed as to the relationship of victim Shaheda Khatun with the sole appellant Labai as husband and wife. To be more clear none of the p.ws. including the two maternal uncles that is, p.ws.1 and 3 stated that deceased Shaheda was married to accused Labai and that they were living together, as husband and wife. And none also deposed that deceased Shaheda was seen with accused Labai on the fateful night. Although p.w.1 while lodging the First Information Report as the informant stated the story of illicit relationship between the victim and the accused and then the marriage between them 17/18 days before of the occurrence, yet while he deposed as p.w.l said nothing to the said effect. Rather p.w.1 categorically stated to the effect that Shaheda was married to one Abdul Mannan of village Monibpur but the learned Additional Sessions Judge totally ignored this very material and vital piece of evidence of p.w.1 and proceeded on a wrong premise that accused Labai was the husband of the deceased and since he was absconding he failed to explain as to how the deceased had met with the death, so he was responsible for the killing of the deceased. It appears that in order to establish the fact that accused appellant Labai was the husband of the deceased the learned Additional Sessions Judge took the clue from the evidence of p.ws 10 and 17 as already stated hereinbefore. So, as of necessity we are to consider as to whether the evidence of p.ws 10 and 17 are sufficient to fix the relationship between the accused-appellant Labai and the deceased Shaheda as husband and wife and thus find him guilty of the charge under section 302 of the Penal Code. But before considering the evidence of the said two witnesses as indicated above we are to consider another pertinent question, namely, as to whether the trial court, that is, the learned Additional Sessions Judge could suo-moto recall the said two prosecution witnesses after they were tendered by the prosecution and the defence declined to cross examine them. It appears that the prosecution closed its evidence on 12.6.91 and on the same day the accused persons who were present in court were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and then next date was fixed for argument on 17.6.91. And on this date pws 10 and 17 were recalled suo-moto by the learned Additional Sessions Judge vide order No.31 and they were examined on 7.7.91 as apparent from order No. 32. The said two orders are as under: 

 22. Thus, it is clear that p.ws.10, 17 and 25 were examined at the instance of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, and of them p.ws.10 and 17 on being re-called. Section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has empowered a court to summon any person as a witness, or examine any person in attendance, though not summoned as a witness, or recall and re-examine any person already examined at any stage of any inquiry, trial or other proceeding under the Code, if his evidence appears to it essential to the just decision of the case. So the precondition to recall or re-examine a witness is that he or she has already been examined. In the instant case as already stated above, both the said p.ws., that is, 10 and 17 were tendered by the prosecution. We are of the view that tendering of a witness by no means can be taken or accepted as examination. Moreso, when the defence declines to cross-examine a witness. And further re-call of a witness always presupposes re-examination. In this regard we may profitably refer to sections 137 and 138 of the Evidence Act. Section 137 of the Evidence Act has defined Examination-In-Chief, Cross-Examination and Re-examination. Here we are concerned with the terminology re-examination which has been defined as under: 

 Section 138 of the Evidence Act has dealt with the order of examination of witnesses which is as under: 

 Thus reading sections 137 and 138 of the Evidence Act together it is clear that even re-examination of a witness shall be at the instance of the party who called him. The other section which empowers a judge to put question to a witness or order for production of any document or thing is section 165 of the Evidence Act which is as under: 

 Provided also that this section shall not authorise any judge to compel any witness to answer any question or to produce any document which such witness would be entitled to refuse to answer or produce under sections 121 to 131, both inclusive, if the question were asked or the document were called for by the adverse party; nor shall the Judge ask any question which it would be improper for any other person to ask under section 148 or 149; nor shall he dispense with primary evidence of any document, except in the cases hereinbefore excepted". 

 23. Now let us examine what p.ws. 10 and 17 proved and whether the learned Additional Sessions Judge was correct in relying upon their evidence in finding the appellant guilty of the charge brought against him under section 302 of the Penal Code. On being recalled by the learned Additional Sessions Judge both the said witnesses in unequivocal language stated that they knew nothing about the occurrence then the prosecution after declaring them hostile put to them the statements allegedly made by them before the Upazilla Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the form of suggestions which they denied but unfortunately the suggestions put to them have been accepted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge as substantive evidence in coming to the finding that Labai was the husband of the deceased Shahed and he killed her as he was last seen with Shahed as per statement of p.w.17. It further appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has treated the said statements of p.ws. 10 and 17 as confessional statements as if they were the accused in the case. The learned Additional Sessions Judge totally failed to consider the categorical statement made by those two witness to the effect that they were tortured by the police and the police further threatened them with more torture if they did not make the statement as dictated by them and that Daroga was present when they made the statement. The learned Additional session Judge also failed to consider that the said p.ws. further asserted that the statements recorded by the Upazila Hakim were not read over to them. The learned Additional Sessions Judge totally ignored the admission of p.w. 25, the Upazilla Magistrate in his cross examination to the effect that column No.8 in the printed form in which the statements of the witnesses were recorded were not filled up and that there was no certificate to the effect that the witnesses made the statements voluntarily and that after recording their statements the same were read over to them. The admission of p.w.25 shows that the alleged statements made by p.ws. 10 and 17 under section 164 of the Code of Criminal procedure were not recorded as per the made of the said section. When the statement allegedly made by a witness was not recorded by the Magistrate as per the mandate of law and the person who allegedly made such statement did not own the same when he deposed in court we fail to understand how such statement could be accepted as a substantive evidence to find an accused guilty of the charge of a grievous offence like 302 of the Penal Code. 

 Even if for argument's sake we accept that p.ws. 17 and 10 made the statements as recorded by the Upazilla Magistrate it cannot be said that the said statements conclusively proved the fact that deceased Shaheda was the wife of accused Labai and they lived together as husband and wife, particularly in the face of the positive evidence through p.w. 1, the informant, the maternal uncle of the deceased in cross examination that deceased Shaheda was married to one Abdul Mannan of village Manibpur. It is by now a settled proposition of law that the statement made by a witness under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be used as substantiate evidence in finding the guilt of an accused. At best it can lend support to the other evidence but when the maker of such statement appearing in court did not own the same and when the recording there of was not made in compliance with the provisions section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the evidentiary value of such statements came to nill. But the learned Additional Sessions Judge totally failed to consider these legal aspects of the case and thus fell into an error in relying on the statements of p.ws. 10 and 17 made before the Upazilla Magistrate as substantive evidence in coming to the finding that the deceased Shaheda was the wife of accused Labi and that the deceased having been seen lastly with him as deposed by p.w.17 he was responsible for her killing. 

 25. It is true that deceased, Shaheda was killed brutally as is evident from the evidence of p.ws .1 — 3, p.w.20 who held the post mortem examination of the deceased and p.w.24 who prepared the inquest report. But the prosecution failed to establish any link or chain of the appellant Labai with the killing of Shaheda by adducing legal evidence as discussed above and, such, he is entitled to be acquitted from the charge brought against him under section 302 of the Penal Code, consequently the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge cannot be sustained.
